title: Scheduler-Attention Handshake Regression — Closure & Preventive Action Plan
creator: Asha Menon
description: Summary: On 2026-03-11 we observed a sustained P95 token generation latency regression (~1.8x) for a subset of medium-length chat workloads. The regression correlated with a rollout of a scheduler change that altered when attention-tiling hints are passed to the kernel selector. Root cause: a timing/handshake mismatch where the scheduler occasionally forwarded requests before the attention tiling metadata was populated, causing the kernel selector to choose a conservative dense-attention kernel rather than the optimized tiled kernel. This increased compute and memory pressure leading to longer queues and higher P95. Scope: ~4% of overall host traffic, concentrated on models with sequence lengths 512-1024 and batching enabled. Immediate impact: customer-facing latency spikes, a handful of customer support tickets, and automated SLA margin alerts. Goal: close the incident with targeted fixes, verify rollbacks and roll-forward safety, and implement guards to prevent recurrence.

mitigation_notes: 2026-03-11 09:40 UTC: Rolled back scheduler change in canary pool which reduced P95 by ~40% within 20 minutes
2026-03-11 10:15 UTC: Enabled a temporary conservative heuristic that forces tiled-kernel when sequence length and kv-cache flags match known pattern; reduced regression scope
Traffic policy: temporarily route affected traffic to dedicated hosts running prior stable kernel-selector until hotfix release is deployed
investigation_notes: Repro: synthetic harness shows that if scheduler enqueues request <10ms before tiling metadata arrives, kernel selector evaluates with missing hint and chooses fallback kernel
Telemetry: kernel_choice_histogram for affected hosts shifted from 72% tiled -> 28% tiled during window; KV cache miss rate increased from 3% -> 12%
Heap/profile: observed 15% higher GPU memory transient due to non-tiling kernel working set; scheduler queue depth increased by median 1.6x
Logs: correlation_id samples show 'tiling_meta: null' immediately prior to dispatch in 6% of sampled requests; root cause tied to a race introduced by optimizing the scheduler batch coalescing path
Patch hypothesis: add explicit fence in scheduler when tiling metadata is asynchronously populated, or modify kernel selector to re-evaluate when metadata arrives within short window
